newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid lack of direction.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid lack of direction.

text.p: Light distillates were steady on Tuesday amid lack of firm direction from crude or Japan, during its holiday.
The naphtha swaps market for May and June stayed in contango with May unchanged at $21.35/$21.55 per barrel and June at $21.45/$21.65.
"The prompt market is weak because of turnarounds in Japan," a major said.
Traders said Indonesian barrels of heavy and N+A naphtha lifting in May were heard sold on term rather than on the spot market due to low premiums talked.
They said premiums were around 35 cents per barrel for fob Singapore cargoes.
Fob 95-octane unleaded gasoline was bid at $24.10 per barrel for May 20-25 lifting while the offer was lower at $23.95 but for May 24-28.

On Monday, end-May lifting barrels of unleaded 95-octane gasoline were offered at $24.14 per barrel, fob by a Japanese trader, while 92-octane unleaded was bid and offered respectively by a Dutch trader and the Japanese trader at $23.60, but for different timings.

Traders said regional demand was still lacklustre although some said Oman had issued a tender to buy two 200,000-barrel cargoes of 97-octane unleaded gasoline but for very prompt May 6 and May 12 delivery.
